reproduction_target: HRDTimer: SBS1-based molecular-time estimation of homologous-recombination-deficiency (HRD) onset and whole-genome-duplication (WGD) timing across 118 HRD+WGD breast/ovarian cancer genomes from three re-used bulk WGS cohorts (PCAWG, SCANB, INFORM/TBCRC-031), plus translation of molecular time to calendar age via SBS1-acceleration models, plus re-analysis of published single-cell duplex sequencing (scNanoSeq, 781 cells / 21 breast cancers) including a duplex power-correction framework and the HRDscout single-cell HRD Random-Forest classifier. No new wet-lab experiment is performed by this study; every input dataset is re-used from prior publications.
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-tool/analysis-invocation, derived from the bioRxiv JATS Methods prose (fetched by curl; WebFetch on the .source.xml returned HTTP 403, curl with a browser UA returned 200 / 209825 bytes; presence of the title string verified in the fetched XML before scoring) plus the GitHub landing page and README prose for github.com/michandreop/HRDTimer. Stage-1 prose-only: no workflow source, no notebook, no environment.yml content was read line-by-line; env_capture_class is 'n/a' on every step and R-star is not assignable. |W| = 0: the study performs no wet-lab step of its own (all sequencing was done in the cited source publications), so there are no OOS steps and computational coverage is 100%. Version-axis convention follows the survey's established practice: a named tool with NO version anywhere in prose or README scores version=0 (Unknown); an exact pin without environment closure scores version=1 (exact_pins_partial); an unpinned-but-declared dependency scores version=1/floating. Steps executed inside the README-declared micromamba environment (hrdtimer_env, created by setup_environment.sh from environment.yml, with MuSiCal pinned via MUSICAL_REF=v1.0.0) are credited version=1 with subflags lock-present-unexecuted + capture-static-only: at Stage 1 the environment file is a CLAIM only, and the guide caps version at 1 without a Stage-2 static-closure check. Neither the paper nor the README pins a HRDTimer release tag or commit, and the landing page shows no release — hence workflow-ref-unpinned on every HRDTimer step (repo is live at 109 commits with 2 open PRs, i.e. a moving target).

steps.label: PCAWG consensus somatic SNV retrieval + PASS filtering (ICGC data portal, .vcf dated '20160830'; consensus requires >=2 of 4 callers: CaVEMan v1.5.1, MuTect, MuSE v1.0rc, DKFZ)
PCAWG consensus somatic indel retrieval (merge of Platypus v0.7.4, cgpPindel v1.5.7, SvABA)
PCAWG consensus allele-specific copy-number profiles (dated '20170119', ICGC data portal) used as timing substrate
PCAWG structural-variant and CNV calls from Hartwig Medical Foundation (GRIDSS v2.9.3, PURPLE v2.53)

SCANB TNBC retrieval (Mendeley 10.17632/2mn4ctdpxp.3) + sample curation/QC: Ascat-vs-Battenberg ploidy concordance within 0.2, purity >= 0.45, coverage >= 25x, HRDetect > 0.7, MutationTimeR classWGD, and MANUAL curation of copy-number profiles / Ascat.Curation exclusions (49 of 233 retained)
INFORM (TBCRC-031, NCT01670500) somatic SNV/indel/CN calling with Sentieon TNScope v202112.01 on 33 tumour/normal WGS pairs (median 38x)
INFORM structural/copy-number calling (GRIDSS v2.13.2, PURPLE v3.8.1) + PURPLE QCStatus 'noisy' exclusion (19/33 pass, 8 WGD-positive retained)
ICGC matched primary-relapse WGS mutation calls with total CN and multiplicity annotations, 7 patients (Mendeley 10.17632/g7kpzkhz8c.1; 'no further filtering of the mutation set was performed')
Pre-malignant breast epithelium: somatic point-mutation calls from 32 single-cell-derived organoids of 12 premenopausal women, 'provided by the study authors' (no accession stated)

scNanoSeq input acquisition: mutation calls, read counts, unique DNA-fragment counts and copy-number profiles for 781 cells 'obtained from the authors of the study' (raw reads separately in SRA PRJNA958124 / PRJNA962101)

Germline-contamination re-profiling of every bulk somatic dataset against gnomAD v2.1 across decreasing population allele-frequency thresholds; choice of the UNFILTERED SCANB call set over the dbSNP v147/ExAC03/dbNSFP3.0a-filtered version
Bulk mutational-signature fitting with MuSiCal (COSMIC v3p2 signature set SBS1/2/3/5/8/13/17a/17b/18/34/51/60, likelihood objective, sparsity likelihood threshold 0.001)
Per-mutation signature-posterior computation P(S|C) from sample-level exposures and normalised 96-channel signature vectors
Whole-genome-duplication classification with MutationTimeR 'classWGD' (genome-wide ploidy + LOH fraction)

Mutation timing against copy-number gains with MutationTimeR 'mutationTime' (1000 bootstraps, all mutations regardless of signature) + search over t in [0,1] for the WGD time that makes most of the genome consistently timed

Sample QC/curation before HRDTimer: MutationTimeR tail-probability check against [0.005,0.995] / [0.025,0.975]; HRDetect bootstrap 95% lower bound > 0.7 (or >= 40% microhomology indels); exclusion when late-SBS1 CI includes zero or mean SBS1 < 15; manual exclusion of INFORM Patient 101 (60 of 91 breast cases retained)

HRDTimer estimation of SBS1-based molecular time of WGD: pi_late per (2,0)/(2,1)/(2,2) copy-number state from [C>T]pG SBS1-weighted mutations, MutationTimeR ploidy normalisation, weighted mean over states (Eq. 1-6)
HRDTimer estimation of SBS1-based molecular time of HRD onset: post-WGD SBS3:SBS1 rate c, correction of early SBS1 count, ploidy-normalised per-state estimates and weighted mean (Eq. 7-14)

Bootstrap confidence intervals for t_WGD and t_HRD: multinomial resampling of the Early/Late/Undefined mutation profiles, re-fitting signatures per resample, 200 iterations, mean + 95% CI (no random seed stated)
Timing of HRD-attributed indels (ID6/ID8) as early/late from PCAWG consensus-indel variant allele fractions via MutationTimeR

Timing of HRD-attributed structural variants from PURPLE/GRIDSS allele-specific CN steps: deletion/tandem-duplication footprint < 100 kb, background major CN in (1.7,2.3), minor CN within 0.3 of integer and of its neighbour, left/right CN-step ratio in (0.7,1.3), mean |CN step| in (0,2); |step|=2 -> early, =1 -> late; stratified by background minor CN 0/1/2
Effective-genome-size estimation from SBS1-weighted mutation multiplicity and rescaling of observed burden to diploid-equivalent burden

Linear regression of normalised SBS1 burden on age (R 'lm', intercept not constrained to zero; age the only continuous covariate, all others categorical; yields 1.54 SBS1 mutations/year in normal breast epithelium)

Molecular-time-to-age translation under three models (linear; tumour-growth two-phase; metastasis-growth two-phase) with r1 = 0.0002569 mutations/Mb/year, 30-fold maximum acceleration line, and m_diag = m_MRCA + delta_m with delta_m = 116 SBS1 mutations

Derivation of chronological tumour-growth time g from published doubling times T_d and diameters T_s (Table S1), assuming spherical growth from D0 = 0.01 mm (10 um); yields 10.5 y for ER- and 16.3 y for ER+ tumours
scNanoSeq tumour/non-tumour cell classification from a CellPhy lineage tree with manual 'long trunk' selection following the original publication; descendants of the trunk called tumour cells
scNanoSeq consensus truncal CNV profiles from previously published Ginkgo single-cell copy-number profiles (retain regions where per-tumour-cell CN standard deviation < 0.5)
scNanoSeq inter-individual contamination screen: overlap of per-cell somatic calls with gnomAD v2.1 across decreasing allele frequencies; exclude cells with > 40% overlap at population AF 0.001

scNanoSeq SNV re-filtering that differs from the original publication: remove variants overlapping gnomAD v2.1 with population AF > 0.001 (replacing dbSNP), and require >= 20x matched-normal coverage (replacing 10x)

scNanoSeq somatic indel calling: samtools mpileup on filtered a4s2 molecules, then two CUSTOM PYTHON SCRIPTS (>= 2 supporting reads per DNA strand, >= 8 bp from read ends, >= 10x matched normal with 0 supporting reads, no indel within 20 bp) and dbSNP v20151104 filtering

Duplex-sequencing power correction of per-cell mutation burden (framework given only in the Supplementary Note 'A mathematical framework for power correction of duplex sequencing assays'); applied in CN 1-5 regions, burden scaled by 3000/c and by 1/(1-d) for low-coverage normal regions, then by effective genome size x2
scNanoSeq coverage-uniformity assessment across trinucleotide contexts vs the reference human genome (GCA depletion traced to the HpyCH4V TGCA motif); no trinucleotide correction applied as a result

De-novo mutational-signature discovery on scNanoSeq via three groupings (per cell with overlaps; per phylogenetic-tree edge using CellPhy assignments; branch-level sets combined with 800 bulk WGS breast cancers), yielding denovo(SBS169-like)

Single-cell signature fitting with MuSiCal (likelihood threshold 0.001) per tumour cell and pooled across non-tumour cells, plus a downsampling simulation of detection sensitivity from the full per-sample mutation set
Per-cell SBS1 burden estimation (power-corrected burden x normalised SBS1 exposure) and MRCA SBS1 burden from intersection with bulk-defined clonal mutations in the 6 samples with matched deep WGS

HRDscout training: Random Forest on 847 bulk WGS breast cancers (breast-560 + SCANB + INFORM) down-sampled to scNanoSeq sensitivity, HRDetect >= 0.7 binary labels, 10-fold cross-validation, ROC/AUC, operating threshold 0.6 (FPR ~0.02), SHAP feature attribution (no library, no hyperparameters, no seed stated)
HRDscout application to single-cell mutation catalogs to assign per-cell HRD probabilities

Germline pathogenic-variant annotation in the scNanoSeq cohort with VEP against Ensembl v112 (GRCh37) and ClinVar 20241001, selecting BRCA1/BRCA2/PALB2 variants pathogenic in the CLNSIG field (VEP software version itself not stated)
Lineage-tree visualisation with the Biopython Phylo module (v1.7.1)

headline.static_readiness: 0/39 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification). Unexecuted; the declared environment (environment.yml + setup_environment.sh creating hrdtimer_env) is a CLAIM read from README prose only, not statically validated and not verified as the environment that produced the results. This zero under-claims by construction: Tier-1 cannot credit an undeclared-but-present dependency, and here it also cannot credit a declared-but-unread lockfile. n_exact_capture_unexecuted = 0, n_fetch_required = 0 (env_capture_class deliberately 'n/a' on all 39 steps under funnel_stage stage1-prose-only).
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: readiness upper bound 21/39 (54%) of computational steps at RI ceiling. The 21 RI steps are those carrying either an exact prose version pin (CaVEMan 1.5.1, MuSE 1.0rc, Platypus 0.7.4, cgpPindel 1.5.7, GRIDSS 2.9.3/2.13.2, PURPLE 2.53/3.8.1, Sentieon TNScope 202112.01, gnomAD v2.1, COSMIC v3p2, dbSNP v20151104, Ensembl v112/GRCh37, ClinVar 20241001, Biopython 1.7.1) or coverage by the claimed hrdtimer_env micromamba environment with MuSiCal pinned at v1.0.0. 16/39 cap at NI, dominated by MutationTimeR (no version anywhere: it is the load-bearing timing engine for C14/C15/C16/C20 and is explicitly NOT installed by setup_environment.sh - the README tells the user to run it themselves via scripts/run_timer.R), by unpinned upstream CN callers (Battenberg, Ascat, HRDetect), by CellPhy and Ginkgo, and by two manual-curation gates (SCANB copy-number curation, scNanoSeq trunk selection) that are irreducibly non-deterministic. 2/39 are X: the INFORM/TBCRC-031 clinical-trial WGS variant-calling steps, whose raw sequence data is neither accessioned nor accompanied by a documented data-access-committee path anywhere in the paper. Never read as 'reproducible' - Tier-1 measures readiness only.
headline.coverage: 39/39 computational steps assessed (100%) from bioRxiv JATS Methods prose + GitHub landing page + README prose. |W| = 0: this study performs no wet-lab step of its own; all sequencing was carried out in the cited source publications, so there are no OOS steps and computational coverage |S|/(|S|+|W|) = 1.00. Stage-2 code verification of the repository (environment.yml closure, example_workflow.ipynb, src/hrdtimer, hrdscout, scripts/run_timer.R) is NOT part of this assessment.

gaps.where: Whole HRDTimer analysis stack (README 'Installation' + repository landing page)
gaps.missing: An environment specification is CLAIMED but not verified at Stage 1. The landing page lists environment.yml, setup_environment.sh and pyproject.toml; the README states 'bash setup_environment.sh ... creates the hrdtimer_env micromamba environment and installs all dependencies (including MuSiCal and the reference genomes) and the hrdtimer package itself', with MUSICAL_REF defaulting to the git tag v1.0.0. Whether environment.yml pins interpreter version, channels/package sources, and declared platforms - i.e. whether it achieves environment closure and is a lock rather than a loose spec - cannot be determined from prose. Under rubric v0.2.5 this caps version at 1 for every step and static_readiness at 0.
gaps.how_to_close: Ship a resolved lock (conda-lock / pixi.lock / micromamba env export --explicit) for each declared platform, or a container image referenced by digest, and state the platform coverage in the README.

gaps.where: C14, C15, C16, C20 - MutationTimeR, the load-bearing timing engine for the entire study
gaps.missing: [gap subtype 2a: version not recorded] MutationTimeR carries no version anywhere: not in the Methods, not in the Data and Code Availability statement, not in the README. Reference 45 cites only 'Gerstung Lab (2024). MutationTimeR. GitHub repository. Accessed: October 22, 2024' - an access date, not a commit or release. The README explicitly places MutationTimeR OUTSIDE the hrdtimer_env environment ('One of HRDTimer's preprocessing steps involves running MutationTimeR on the VCFs of interest ... An example of how to implement MutationTimeR yourself can be found in the script: /scripts/run_timer.R'), and the tutorial ships pre-processed VCFs so the step is never exercised end-to-end by the example workflow. No R version is stated either. Every downstream molecular-time estimate depends on this unpinned preprocessing.
gaps.how_to_close: Pin MutationTimeR to a commit SHA or release tag, state the R version and R package versions (renv.lock or sessionInfo), and bring the preprocessing step inside the declared environment.

gaps.where: C3, C5, C23, C26, C27, C31, C32, C35 - unpinned or unnamed tooling
gaps.missing: [gap subtype 2a: version not recorded] No version for: Battenberg, Ascat, HRDetect (SCANB curation and HRD calling), the PCAWG consensus copy-number algorithm, R and R's lm (SBS1-vs-age regression), CellPhy (lineage tree), Ginkgo (single-cell CN), samtools (scNanoSeq indel mpileup), and the scikit-learn / SHAP libraries behind HRDscout. These steps cannot reach RI on the version axis.
gaps.how_to_close: Record exact versions (and builds) for every named tool in a Methods versions table, and include the R/Bioconductor stack in the shipped environment capture.

gaps.where: Data and Code Availability statement vs the scNanoSeq re-analysis (C26-C35)
gaps.missing: The availability statement scopes the deposit narrowly: 'Code for HRDTimer and the analysis of bulk whole genome samples is available through https://github.com/michandreop/HRDTimer/'. The single-cell re-analysis - CellPhy trunk selection, Ginkgo consensus truncal CN, gnomAD contamination screening, the duplex power-correction implementation, per-cell SBS1 burden and MRCA intersection - is not claimed to be deposited, even though the landing page shows a data_scNanoSeq/ directory and an hrdscout/ directory whose contents were not read at Stage 1.
gaps.how_to_close: Extend the availability statement to name the single-cell analysis code explicitly, or state which parts are intentionally not released.

gaps.missing: Two filtering stages are described as 'a custom Python script' with no deposit location. The numeric criteria are fully specified in prose (>= 2 reads per strand, >= 8 bp from read ends, >= 10x normal coverage with 0 supporting reads, no indel within 20 bp, dbSNP v20151104), so the step is re-implementable, but the executed code is not available.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the indel-calling and indel-filtering scripts in the HRDTimer repository.

gaps.where: C6, C7 - INFORM / TBCRC-031 clinical-trial whole-genome sequencing
gaps.missing: No accession and no data-access-committee path is given for the INFORM WGS data (33 tumour/normal pairs from NCT01670500). The Data and Code Availability section exposes only a Chromoscope visualisation configuration for the HRD+WGD subset (https://chromoscope.bio/app/?external=https://somatic-browser-test.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/inform/INFORM_config_hrdtiming.json), which is a browser configuration for derived somatic calls, not a deposited primary dataset with a resolvable accession. The variant-calling steps on this cohort are therefore unrecoverable (X).
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the INFORM WGS in a controlled-access archive (dbGaP/EGA) with the DAC application path documented, or state explicitly that raw data cannot be shared and provide the derived call sets under a citable accession.

gaps.where: C9, C10 - pre-malignant organoid calls and scNanoSeq per-cell matrices
gaps.missing: The 32 single-cell-derived organoid mutation calls were 'provided by the study authors' and the 781-cell scNanoSeq mutation calls, read counts, unique-fragment counts and copy-number profiles were 'obtained from the authors of the study'. Neither is given an accession in this paper. The scNanoSeq RAW reads are accessioned (SRA PRJNA958124, PRJNA962101), but the actual analysis inputs are derived matrices obtained by private request, and the filtering applied here differs from the original publication.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the exact derived input matrices used (per-cell mutation calls, coverage/fragment counts, copy-number profiles, organoid call sets) as a supplementary archive with a DOI.

gaps.where: README 'Install the HRDTimer environment' - clone URL
gaps.missing: The README instructs 'git clone https://github.com/parklab/HRDTimer.git', but that URL returned HTTP 404 on 2026-07-28. The URL that resolves is the one printed in the paper, https://github.com/michandreop/HRDTimer/ (HTTP 200). A user following the README verbatim cannot obtain the code.
gaps.how_to_close: Correct the README clone URL, or make the parklab/HRDTimer canonical repository public before publication.

gaps.where: C1-C4, C6, C7 - upstream variant calling for all three bulk cohorts
gaps.missing: None of the primary variant/CN/SV calling was performed by this study for PCAWG (consensus calls downloaded from the ICGC portal) or Hartwig SV/CN; for INFORM it was performed but the invocation is not deposited. The reproduction entry point is therefore the downloaded call sets, not raw reads, and the sub-pipeline is externalised to consortium infrastructure that no longer exists in its original form (see gap type 3 note on the retired ICGC data portal).
gaps.how_to_close: State the exact download manifest (file names and checksums) of every consortium call set consumed, so that the analysis entry point is byte-identifiable.

gaps.where: C1-C4, C20, C21 - PCAWG consensus call sets
gaps.missing: The Methods acknowledge the link rot directly: 'The ICGC data portal has since been retired, but somatic mutation calls remain accessible from the ICGC Argo website.' Redundancy rescue applies - ICGC ARGO is an authoritative successor and the DACO application path (https://docs.icgc-argo.org/docs/data-access/daco/applying, HTTP 200) is documented - so this is scored as legitimate controlled access (data=2, subflag controlled-access), NOT penalised. Recorded here because the originally cited portal (dcc.icgc.org) no longer serves the dated file releases ('20160830', '20170119') the Methods identify.
gaps.how_to_close: Cite the ARGO-side identifiers for the specific dated releases consumed, since the original portal paths are no longer resolvable to those exact files.

gaps.missing: Sentieon TNScope v202112.01 is commercial proprietary software. It is exactly version-pinned (license-gated -> version=1) but requires a paid licence to execute, so this step is ceiling-capped at NI even before the data gap; combined with the absent raw data it lands at X.
gaps.how_to_close: Provide an open-tool equivalent call set (e.g. Mutect2/Strelka) alongside, or document a licence-free path for reviewers.

gaps.where: C19, C34, C36 - bootstrapping, downsampling simulation, Random Forest
gaps.missing: No random seed is stated for the 200-iteration multinomial bootstrap, for the mutation-downsampling sensitivity simulation, or for the Random Forest training / 10-fold cross-validation split. Reproduction is limited to distributional agreement, not exact reproduction of the reported confidence intervals and AUC.
gaps.how_to_close: Record and expose the RNG seeds (and the RNG implementation) used for each stochastic step.

gaps.where: C11, C28, C29, C30, C38 - external reference resources
gaps.missing: External resources are pinned in PROSE (gnomAD v2.1, dbSNP v20151104, Ensembl v112 / GRCh37, ClinVar 20241001, COSMIC v3p2). Whether the workflow itself fetches these at a pinned version, consumes a user-supplied local path, or pulls a rolling 'latest' cannot be determined without reading the code - so env_capture_class is deliberately left 'n/a' and no A/B/C classification is asserted. The README's claim that setup_environment.sh 'installs ... the reference genomes' is the single strongest reason this paper warrants Stage-2: it is exactly the aMeta failure mode (env lock present, DB pinning absent) that Stage-1 prose cannot distinguish.
gaps.how_to_close: Make every reference-resource download an explicit versioned rule in the workflow (versioned URL/DOI or digest), so the pin lives in code rather than in prose.

gaps.where: C5, C16, C26 - manual curation gates
gaps.missing: Three decision points are human judgements that no environment capture can restore: 'manual curation of copy number profiles to ensure closeness to integer levels' (SCANB), exclusion of samples where 'a higher-than-expected fraction of mutations had tail probabilities outside these intervals' (threshold not numerically defined) plus the individually reasoned exclusion of INFORM Patient 101, and selection of 'a long trunk' on the CellPhy tree. The 118-sample cohort and the 60/91 high-confidence breast subset are partly the product of these judgements.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish the resulting per-sample include/exclude table with the reason per sample, so the curated cohort is reconstructable even where the judgement is not.
